origin.description: Restore an object written by serializeJSON.
origin.details: Environments and most languages objects are outside this mapping.
origin.example:
obj <- unserializeJSON(serializeJSON(list(a = 1L, b = "x")))
cat(paste(obj$a, obj$b), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Reads the type tag and rebuilds lists, atomics, and raw bytes.
translation.details: A length-one atomic vector is returned as that one value.
translation.example:
from jsonlite import serializeJSON, unserializeJSON
obj = unserializeJSON(serializeJSON({"a": 1, "b": "x"}))
print(f"{obj['a']} {obj['b']}")
